home.content:
Abstract fluid art · Akron, Ohio

Walk In, See the Work, Take One Home.

Fluid, layered abstract work — made by hand, and seen in person at my studio inside Salon Lofts.

View the work Visit the studio
Selected work

A few recent pieces.

View all work →
Canyon RiversSoft ribbons of warm taupe, bronze, copper, ivory, charcoal, and muted gold drift across a crisp white canvas, creating the appearance of natural stone shaped over time. Delicate lacing and translucent layers add depth and texture, while sweeping organic lines guide the eye through the composition. The balance of movement and open space evokes a sense of calm, quiet luxury, and the beauty of nature's imperfections.
NoirNoir is a bold abstract composition where deep black, soft white, and smoky gray flow together with unexpected bursts of vibrant magenta. Organic forms bloom and dissolve across the canvas, creating a striking balance between strength and softness. Layered textures, delicate lacing, and fluid movement evoke ink suspended in water or petals unfolding in shadow. Both dramatic and elegant, the painting invites viewers to discover new shapes and emotions with every look.
Green GoddessGreen Goddess celebrates the vitality and quiet power of nature through flowing shades of emerald, teal, turquoise, and soft white. Organic forms unfurl across the canvas like blooming leaves, ocean currents, or lush botanical life, while intricate cellular textures add depth and movement. The balance of vibrant color and open white space creates a sense of renewal, serenity, and effortless grace, inviting the viewer to pause and reconnect with the natural world.
Made by hand

Poured, layered, guided by movement.

Each piece is built through fluid color and the small surprises that happen when paint is allowed to move.

schema.name: How an acrylic pour painting is made
schema.description: Elizabeth Zab's fluid-art process: a poured palette, shaped by tilt and warm air, then a long slow dry.

step.name: Pour the palette
step.text: Mixed acrylic paint is poured directly onto the canvas in a chosen palette.

step.name: Shape with tilt and movement
step.text: The canvas is tilted so gravity and movement carry the paint into flowing, organic shapes.

step.name: Open the cells with warm air
step.text: Warm air from a hairdryer opens cells in the paint and shapes how the pigments settle.

step.name: Slow dry and finish by hand
step.text: The piece dries slowly, then is signed and dated by hand on the back of the canvas.

story.content:
The story

A painting is a kind of dance.

I'm Elizabeth, an abstract artist working primarily in acrylic pouring and fluid art techniques, from a studio inside Salon Lofts in Akron. My work is guided by a deep connection to color, movement, and the organic flow of paint as it finds its own shape on canvas.

"The hairdryer is part of the process. It moves the paint, opens the cells, and gives each piece its breath."

I approach painting as a kind of dance. Every piece begins with a poured palette and ends with a careful tilt, a quiet breath of warm air, and a long slow dry. No two are alike. Each is signed, dated, and finished by hand on the back of the canvas.

My work is inspired by the Japanese philosophy of wabi-sabi: finding beauty in imperfection, simplicity, and the natural flow of life. Each painting embraces movement, organic details, and subtle variations that cannot be repeated, making every piece truly one of a kind.

Want to see the process in person?

Walk in from the Salon Lofts lobby in Akron to see how a pour painting comes together.

acceptedAnswer.text: Acrylic pour painting, also known as fluid art, is a contemporary painting technique in which acrylic paints are mixed with a pouring medium to create a smooth, flowing consistency. The paint is then poured and layered onto the canvas, allowing the colors to move, blend, and interact organically. The Dutch pour is a fluid art technique that uses air to guide the paint across the canvas. By blowing and directing the colors, the artist creates flowing movement, delicate details, and one-of-a-kind abstract compositions. Because the paint moves naturally, each piece develops its own unique character and cannot be recreated exactly.
Warm air opens cells in the paint and helps me shape how the pigments settle. It's part of how each piece finds its breath. It's also how I keep the paint moving without losing its body.

mainEntity.name: Can I commission a custom piece?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. I take commissions for specific palettes, sizes, and rooms. Most commissions take two to four weeks depending on size and cure time. Reach out by phone or Instagram to start.

mainEntity.name: Can I pick up at the studio?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — local pickup at the Salon Lofts studio in Akron is the easiest way. Walk in during my studio hours, or message me on Instagram to schedule.

Shipping or pickup can be discussed when you inquire. Most local buyers (Akron, Cleveland, Medina, Hudson) pick up directly at the studio, which is the easiest option. International shipping is not offered at this time.

mainEntity.name: Do you offer Certificates of Authenticity?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every original ships with a signed Certificate of Authenticity that includes the piece's title, date, materials, and a brief note about the work.

mainEntity.name: Do you work with realtors or designers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. I work with realtors and interior designers on staging listings with original work, commissioning palettes to match a room, and signed originals as client gifts. See the designers & realtors page, or call (440) 477-1972.

mainEntity.name: Where can I see the work in person?

acceptedAnswer.text: At my studio inside Salon Lofts, 3987 Medina Rd, Studio 3, Akron, OH 44333. Walk in during studio hours to see the work in person.

qa.content:
Common questions

Good to know.

Common questions about the work, the studio, and how to buy.

What Is Fluid Art?

Acrylic pour painting, also known as fluid art, is a contemporary painting technique in which acrylic paints are mixed with a pouring medium to create a smooth, flowing consistency. The paint is then poured and layered onto the canvas, allowing the colors to move, blend, and interact organically.

The Dutch pour is a fluid art technique that uses air to guide the paint across the canvas. By blowing and directing the colors, the artist creates flowing movement, delicate details, and one-of-a-kind abstract compositions.

Because the paint moves naturally, each piece develops its own unique character and cannot be recreated exactly.

What is the hairdryer for?

Warm air opens cells in the paint and helps me shape how the pigments settle. It's part of how each piece finds its breath. It's also how I keep the paint moving without losing its body.

Can I commission a custom piece?

Yes. I take commissions for specific palettes, sizes, and rooms. Most commissions take two to four weeks depending on size and cure time. Reach out by phone or Instagram to start.

Can I pick up at the studio?

Yes — local pickup at the Salon Lofts studio in Akron is the easiest way. Walk in during my studio hours, or message me on Instagram to schedule.

Do you ship?

Shipping or pickup can be discussed when you inquire. Most local buyers (Akron, Cleveland, Medina, Hudson) pick up directly at the studio, which is the easiest option. International shipping is not offered at this time.

Do you offer Certificates of Authenticity?

Every original ships with a signed Certificate of Authenticity that includes the piece's title, date, materials, and a brief note about the work.

Do you work with realtors or designers?

Yes. I work with realtors and interior designers on staging listings with original work, commissioning palettes to match a room, and signed originals as client gifts. See the designers & realtors page, or call (440) 477-1972.

Where can I see the work in person?

At my studio inside Salon Lofts, 3987 Medina Rd, Studio 3, Akron, OH 44333. Walk in during studio hours to see the work in person.
